title: Lesson Plan — Number Systems (Class 10 NIOS Mathematics)
subject: Mathematics
objectives: Explain the relationship N ⊂ W ⊂ Z ⊂ Q with at least one example each.
Express a given rational number in standard (lowest) form and identify equivalent rationals.
Perform addition, subtraction, multiplication and division on rational numbers and apply commutative, associative and distributive properties to simplify expressions.
Decide whether a given rational number has a terminating or non-terminating recurring decimal expansion based on its denominator's prime factorisation.
Convert recurring decimals to p/q form using algebraic manipulation.
prerequisites: Familiarity with addition, subtraction, multiplication and division of fractions (Class 8 / 9 level).
Understanding of factors and prime factorisation.
Ability to plot integers and simple fractions on a number line.
materials: Set of cards labelled with numbers from each category (e.g. 7, −3, 0, 2/3, 0.875, √2)
Calculator (one per pair) for cross-checking long divisions

activities.description: Card-sort hook: students sit in pairs and receive a stack of cards. They sort them onto a printed Venn diagram with regions for Natural, Whole, Integer, Rational. The teacher times the activity and asks pairs to defend their placements for two contentious cards (e.g. 0 and 0.875).
teacher_actions: Distribute card stacks and Venn diagrams to each pair.
Walk the room and listen for misconceptions, especially around 0 and negative integers.
Pick two pairs to share their reasoning for 0 and 0.875.
student_actions: Sort cards collaboratively and justify placements verbally.
Note any cards they disagreed about for whole-class discussion.

activities.description: Number-line walk: in pairs, students plot 1/2, −3, 0, 3/4, −5/2 on a 0-centred number line strip. They then write three observations comparing positions, including one ordering claim and one density claim ('I can find a number between any two of these').
teacher_actions: Demonstrate plotting 2/3 and −1.5 on the board first.
Probe pairs with the question 'Can you find a rational strictly between 1/2 and 3/4?' to surface density.
Collect 2-3 student observations and write them on the board.
student_actions: Plot the given numbers, then attempt to add a rational strictly between two existing markers.

activities.description: Direct instruction: the teacher consolidates definitions of N, W, Z, Q with the relationship N ⊂ W ⊂ Z ⊂ Q on the board, derives the standard form of a rational number, and walks through worked examples on adding, multiplying and dividing rationals using a common denominator. The teacher then derives the decimal-expansion rule by long-dividing 7/40 (terminates) and 5/12 (recurs), connecting the result to the prime factorisation of the denominator.
teacher_actions: Build the chain N ⊂ W ⊂ Z ⊂ Q on the board with one example per inclusion.
Work three examples on the board: 2/3 + 5/6, 4/5 × 10/9, and 3/4 ÷ 2/5.
Long-divide 7/40 and 5/12 in front of the class; circle the prime factorisations of 40 and 12.
State the rule: terminates iff denominator (lowest terms) is 2^m × 5^n.
student_actions: Take notes; replicate each worked example in their notebooks.
Predict, before the teacher long-divides, whether 7/40 and 5/12 will terminate.
Add the rule and one example of each kind to a 'rules box' in their notebooks.

activities.description: Application station: students work through five problems from the worksheet on their own — one each on simplifying p/q to lowest terms, evaluating a mixed expression on rationals, finding a rational between two given rationals, predicting termination from the denominator, and converting 0.4̄5̄ to a fraction. The teacher circulates and prompts students who get stuck to verbalise their first step.
teacher_actions: Circulate and use targeted hints rather than full solutions.
Collect common mistakes for the Evaluate phase.
Pair fast finishers with peers who need support.
student_actions: Solve the five problems individually, showing all steps.
Self-check against a posted answer key after the first three.
Ask a peer before asking the teacher.

activities.description: Exit-ticket quiz: a 6-question MCQ + short-answer slip covering each section of the chapter, drawn from the question bank. Students complete it silently in 8 minutes; the teacher then projects the answers and conducts a 4-minute class discussion focused on the two items most students missed.
teacher_actions: Distribute the exit-ticket; remind students it is individual work.
Time the quiz to 8 minutes strictly.
Quickly tally results and address the top two miss items.
student_actions: Self-mark and write a one-line reflection on the item they got wrong, if any.

activities.description: Set homework: complete the remainder of the worksheet, plus one CREATE-level question from the bank ('Construct a recurring decimal whose repeating block has exactly 3 digits and convert it to lowest-terms p/q'). Preview the link to the next chapter (Exponents and Radicals) by writing 8 × 8 × 8 = 8^3 on the board.
teacher_actions: Announce homework due date and the CREATE-level prompt.
Bridge to the next chapter with the 8^3 example.
student_actions: Pack the worksheet for home study.

homework: Complete the remaining problems on the Worksheet — Number Systems handout (problems 6 to 10).
Complete one CREATE-level prompt: invent a 3-digit-block recurring decimal and convert it to lowest-terms p/q, showing the algebra.
Identify, with justification, three textbook fractions whose decimal expansions terminate and three whose expansions recur.
assessment_ideas: Use the 6-item exit ticket described in the Evaluate phase as a quick formative check.
Set a 10-question MCQ quiz drawn from the chapter's question bank for the next class as a summative assessment.
Mark a small subjective response on the prime-factorisation rule (long answer #3 from the bank) using the auto-grade rubric.
Conduct a 5-minute peer-grading round on the CREATE homework using a simple two-criterion rubric (algebra correct? lowest terms?).
references: NIOS Secondary Mathematics, Module 1, Lesson 1: Number Systems.
NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 1: Real Numbers (for cross-board comparison).
